title: Grateful Dead Live at Pauley Pavilion - University of California on 1973-11-17

ai_review.summary: A pristine soundboard capture of a high‑energy November ’73 performance with a smoking Here Comes Sunshine, Row Jimmy, Ramble On Rose and a crystal‑clear Morning Dew.
ai_review.review: The Jay Ashley restoration delivers virtually perfect, crisp sound that lets the band’s soaring energy shine through, from Jerry’s pure surf‑guitar tone on Here Comes Sunshine to Keith’s sparkling piano throughout. Highlights include Row Jimmy, Jack Straw, Ramble On Rose (with Phil’s bombs) and an especially crystalline Morning Dew, while a few minor flubs keep the set from being flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews rate the show 4‑5 stars and praise both performance and recording; only a single negative comment on harsh sound tempers an otherwise excellent consensus.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly describe the audio as crisp, fresh, virtually perfect, with a “peal spritzer” to the ear; one reviewer noted occasional harshness but it is outweighed by overall clarity and balance.

poor_songs: Playin' (start of set noted as train‑wreck)
show_quality.setlist_flow: The first set is tight and energetic, flowing seamlessly into a second set praised for its superb transitions; a few reviewers feel the momentum wanes later in the second half.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Described as being in pure surf‑guitar mode with an “unadulterated” tone, delivering mission‑to‑Mars solos and powerful vocals on several songs.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is highlighted as amazing; Phil’s bombs shine especially on Ramble On Rose.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob Weir’s vocal edge noted on Aroundx2 and his presence praised despite occasional lyric flubs; overall solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano/keyboard work repeatedly called great, sparkling, and a key part of the show’s jazzy feel.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill (drummer) is mentioned as “so good on Jack Straw,” indicating strong, driving drumming throughout.
